title: Haynes King, Panthers’ Hall of Fame Game hero, ‘week-to-week’ with hamstring injury
content:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. — When Carolina Panthers rookie quarterback Haynes King walked off the Arizona Cardinals with a game-winning touchdown run Thursday, it capped what some called the best Hall of Fame Game in recent memory.

The victory also came with a consequence.

King, an undrafted free agent from Georgia Tech, is “week to week” with a hamstring injury, according to a league source who was not authorized to speak publicly on a player’s injury status.

The Panthers’ final exhibition game is against the Houston Texans on Aug. 28, two days before the roster-cut deadline. King is listed behind Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett on the team’s official depth chart.

The Panthers plan to sign another QB while King is sidelined, the source said. They recently worked out Kyle Trask, who was with coach Dave Canales in Tampa. Jack Plummer also could be an option: The UFL MVP spent the 2024 season with Carolina before being waived last summer.

King, the ACC’s Player of the Year in 2025, scrambled for a 5-yard touchdown as time expired in the 33-30 win over the Cardinals in Canton, Ohio. King dropped back looking to throw, but said he took off from the pocket when the middle of the Cardinals’ defense “parted.” With a linebacker angling toward him, King dove and extended the ball across the goal line, setting off a raucous celebration. Teammates rushed to surround King as he stood up.

King didn’t mention the injury during postgame interviews.

King and Cardinals rookie QB Carson Beck — who once dueled in a memorable, eight-overtime game in college — impressed in their NFL debuts. King completed 21 of 34 passes for 180 yards and two TDs, while rushing for 39 yards on three carries. Beck was 15-of-19 passing for 188 yards and a score.

Panthers players and coaches were fired up for the 25-year-old King after his game-winner. As King conducted an on-field interview, defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero walked by and said, “A star is born.” Young wore a big smile, while offensive lineman Rob Hunt noted he and King are both from east Texas.

“I’m very excited I got this opportunity. I feel like I went out there and operated at a high level,” King said afterward. “And I feel like I affected a lot of people and allowed everybody around me to play better as well.”
